did: The landing's Android episode is now a pool of 22 short, first-person snacks about why each app exists: growth through engagement, Rust Rounds, Korean, Studio, Settings and My data, and the interview week, each citing the issue its words rest on. Every visit draws four with the repo's one seeded Fisher-Yates; a reader with no script sees a fixed first draw. A new screen face takes each app's still from Snips Capture's own bundle. The owner approved the preview and the snacks went live with the merge.

calls.title: The pool's shape (C1440)
options: A pool as a case of the episode's scenes, drawn by the landing's script into the first draw's places
A separate snack module beside the show
A draw at build time, so each deploy shows one fixed set
calls.why: It keeps one Show/Episode family any episode can use, reads whole with no script, and draws fresh each visit as the owner asked.
calls.undo: Turn the Android pool back into its four Jobs chapters and drop Pool, Snack, draw.ts, pool-dom.ts, timedScenes and the screen face.

calls.title: A route the capture missed is a warning, not a failed run
options: Warn on the Snips Capture run and in its summary
calls.why: A red capture run would hide its Jobs faces from Pages and its bundle from home, for one missing still; the face shows its title card instead. Listed on #3474.
calls.undo: Make show-faces.ts throw when a named route has no picture.

left: The new screen faces show title cards until a Snips Capture runs on main; the coordinator dispatches one before the Pages deploy.
No clip in paulgsc/testing: this session's GitHub access was scoped to some-ui, and the screens wait on that capture.
The stale-branch footgun (check how far behind main a branch is before waiting on CI) goes into the coordinate and steward skills once the merge queue drains; the coordinator holds it.
